RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, September 6, 2011/Bhadra 15, 1933 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Drinking Water and Sanitation; Environment and Forests;
Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises;Petroleum and Natural Gas; Rural Development)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Non-availability of cheap vaccines
*461. DR E. M. SUDARSANA
NATCHIAPPAN: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has ordered
suspension of manufacturing licences of
three PSUs namely, Central Research
Institute at Kasauli, Pasteur Institute of
India at Coonoor and BCG Vaccine
Laboratory at Chennai in January, 2008;
and
(b) if so, whether their closure has
coincided with non-availability of vaccines
for the poor people and increase of cost of
vaccines by 50-70 per cent by private sector?
Difficulties faced by forest officers
*462. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
difficulties faced by forest officers in the
field due to conflicting provisions of the
Forest Rights Act, the Forest Conservation
Act and the Panchayat (Extension to the
Scheduled Areas) (PESA) Act as well as
guidelines issued by the Ministry; and
(b) the steps being taken for harmonious
interpretation of these laws to resolve the
conflicts on the ground?
World Bank assistance for Rural
Development Projects
†*463. SHRI RANJITSINH
VIJAYSINH MOHITE PATIL: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry
is facing shortage of funds and hence it is
not able to implement its projects;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
Ministry is going to take assistance from
the World Bank for its Flagship Scheme,
viz. National Rural Livelihood Mission
(NRLM);
(c) the names of other projects for
which the Ministry is planning to take
assistance from the World Bank; and

134
(d) the amount of loan sought as soft
loan from the World Bank for all its projects
by the Ministry?
Permanent employment under
MGNREGS
*464. SHRI SHADI LAL BATRA: Will
the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken any
decision to provide permanent
employment under the Mahatma Gandhi
National Rural Employment Guarantee
Scheme (MGNREGS);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps taken by Government in
this regard?
Restrictions on sale of antibiotics
*465. SHRI S. THANGA VELU: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has restricted
the sale of 90 commonly prescribed
antibiotics to put an end to the misuse of
antibiotics;
(b) whether Government has also
restricted sale of 16 medicines to tertiary
care hospitals directly and sale of 74
medicines only on the prescription of
registered medical practitioners;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether All India Organisation of
Chemists and Druggists, the apex body of
over 7 lakh licensed medicines sellers, is
against the move as due to an estimated
loss of business worth ` 5000 crore for the
retail medical stores across the country;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Problems faced by patients at AIIMS
due to renovation works
†*466. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH :
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether six out of twelve Operation
Theatres (OTs) have been kept non-
operational for a long time due to ongoing
renovation works in the main O.T. block at
AIIMS, New Delhi;
(b) if so, by when these closed OTs
would resume functioning and the time-
limit fixed earlier to complete the renovation
works and the revised time-limit now;
(c) whether problems of patients
coming from various parts of the country
have increased due to non-functioning of
these OTs as they are forced to wait
indefinitely for operation; and
(d) the arrangements in place to tackle
day-to-day problems being faced by
patients in AIIMS?
Increase in pension for widows in BPL
category
*467. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of widows of BPL
category in the country who get ` 200 per
month as pension under the Government
scheme, State-wise;
(b) whether BPL widows are adequately
aware of the scheme across India;
(c) whether there is any plan to increase
the amount of pension, which is very
meagre at present; and
(d) whether Government has any other
such scheme for BPL widows?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
